title: Why Transformers Replaced RNNs — Direct Access Has a Memory Price

body:
## Direct Access Has a Memory Price

Every token compares with every other token. Doubling sequence length can create about four times as many comparison scores.

Standard attention therefore has quadratic memory and computation in sequence length. Efficient variants use windows, sparse links, compression, or specialized kernels.

RNNs can still suit streaming and tiny-device tasks because their state updates use steady memory. Architecture choice depends on context length, latency, hardware, and quality.
common_mistakes: Transformers read only the immediately previous token.
Parallel training means token order no longer matters.
Attention has zero memory cost at every sequence length.
